critical_code_review_comments: products.py:track_product uses count_documents + insert_one without a lock — under concurrent 4th-product race two inserts could both pass the check. Low impact given per-user rate & UI serial flow but consider a Mongo find_one_and_update guard or a unique compound sequence.

pc.py health_history filter uses string comparison on ISO timestamps (str(p.get('created_at')) >= cutoff). Works because ISO-8601 UTC strings sort lexicographically, but only if 'created_at' is always stored as ISO string with the same timezone offset. If a doc ever stored as datetime object or with a different offset, this filter breaks silently. Recommend parsing to datetime for the comparison.

plan_gate.get_entitlements does one extra DB read (user_progress.find_one) on every /subscriptions/status call. Not a hotspot today but consider caching within the request (contextvar) since multiple endpoints (missions, milestones, pc router) recompute it per call.

Report.jsx: pdfOk defaults to true and is set from entitlements; if /subscriptions/status is slow, briefly a starter user sees the PDF icon (not lock) before the fetch resolves. Suggest initial pdfOk=false or a small skeleton state to avoid the misleading unlocked flash.

milestones.py: for the secret trophy 'speed_demon', when locked the reward object is masked to None. Frontend consumers looking for reward.key === 'gpu_reference_full' won't find it until the secret is triggered — intentional but worth documenting so the catalog listing UI doesn't fail lookup.
